h: Making a proper seaside day of it
p: Because you pay as you go rather than handing over a big entry fee, Harbour Park is ideal for dipping in and out. A lot of families treat it as the reward at the end of a beach session: a few rides, a go in the arcade, then back to the sand. Set yourselves a budget or a number of rides before you walk in, and nobody ends up negotiating at every turn.

Allow a couple of hours if you're doing it properly with little ones, or less if it's a quick treat. Younger kids tend to want the same favourite ride over and over, so don't rush them on to the next thing. It's that third go they'll remember.

Littlehampton sits where the River Arun meets the sea, and that makes it a lovely place to wander. Stroll along the riverside to watch boats heading in and out, or take in the long sweep of East Beach right next to the park. Over the river, West Beach has sand dunes and a wilder, quieter feel if you fancy a change of scene, though it's a walk round rather than a quick hop.
Got a bit more time? Arundel, with its castle, cathedral and independent shops, is only a short drive or train ride inland and makes a smashing add-on to a Littlehampton trip.

Practical bits: bring a jacket even in summer, because the wind off the sea can be cheeky, and keep some sun cream handy too. Littlehampton has its own railway station, so it's possible to do the day without the car, which takes the stress out of finding somewhere to park on a busy weekend.
